questions.stem: The 'Wangala' — a post-harvest festival of Meghalaya featuring the famous 'hundred drums' ceremony — is primarily celebrated by which tribal community?

options.option_text: Khasi tribe of eastern Meghalaya hills
Garo tribe of western Meghalaya region
Mizo community of southern Mizoram state
Bodo tribe of the lower Assam valley belt

questions.explanation: B is correct. Wangala is the most important festival of the Garo tribe, celebrated after harvest to thank their supreme deity Saljong (the Sun God of fertility and harvest). The 'hundred drums' (asíma) ceremony is its defining feature. The Khasi celebrate Nongkrem Dance; the Mizo celebrate Chapchar Kut; the Bodo celebrate Bwisagu — all common distractors from NE India that students conflate.

questions.stem: The 'Gangaur' festival of Rajasthan is dedicated to Goddess Gauri (Parvati). Women observe this 18-day festival — beginning from Holi — primarily to pray for which blessing?

options.option_text: Fertility of agricultural fields in the rabi harvest
Marital bliss and long life for their beloved husbands
Protection of children from seasonal illnesses and diseases
Prosperity in trade and household wealth all year

questions.explanation: B is correct. 'Gangaur' is derived from 'Gan' (Shiva) and 'Gaur' (Gauri/Parvati). Married women pray for their husbands' longevity and unmarried women pray for a worthy husband, celebrating Parvati's reunion with Shiva after her penance. Options A, C, and D are plausible agricultural or protective themes but belong to other festivals — Gangaur is specifically centred on marital wellbeing.

questions.stem: The Ambubachi Mela at Kamakhya temple (Assam) — one of India's largest tantric gatherings held each June — is timed according to which recurring natural-religious belief?

options.option_text: Goddess Kamakhya undergoes her annual menstrual cycle
The Brahmaputra river sanctifies the hilltop shrine annually
Summer solstice rays align with the temple's sanctum axis
The sacred spring inside the temple overflows each monsoon

questions.explanation: A is correct. Ambubachi Mela marks the annual menstruation of the earth goddess Kamakhya. The temple closes for three days; priests observe strict seclusion; the goddess's menstrual cloth (angavastra) is then distributed as prasad — a distinctive Shakta tantric tradition. Option B (Brahmaputra link) exploits Assam's river association, and C (solstice alignment) sounds scientific but both are incorrect; the festival is entirely tied to the goddess's cyclical symbolism.

questions.stem: The 'Sammakka-Saralamma Jatara' (Medaram Jatara) — believed to be Asia's largest tribal fair commemorating the martyrdom of Koya heroines — is held once every two years. In which state and district does it take place?

options.option_text: Odisha, in the Koraput district forest region
Telangana, in the Mulugu district forest region
Jharkhand, in Deoghar district near the Damodar
Chhattisgarh, in the Bastar district forest belt

questions.explanation: B is correct. Medaram Jatara is held at Medaram village in Mulugu district (carved from Warangal), Telangana, inside Eturnagaram Wildlife Sanctuary. Sammakka and Saralamma are a mother-daughter pair who fought the Kakatiya king and were martyred; the biennial jatara attracts over 1 crore devotees. Options A, C, and D are major tribal-belt states with large fairs, but none hosts this specific jatara — a precise district-level recall question.

questions.stem: During Puri's Rath Yatra, Jagannath's chariot is 'Nandighosha' and Balabhadra's is 'Taladhwaja'. What is Goddess Subhadra's chariot called, and which symbol appears on its flag?

options.option_text: Darpadalana, with a lotus (Padma) on the flag
Devadalana, with a conch-shell emblem on the flag
Padmadhwaja, with an eight-hooded serpent on the flag
Garududhwaja, with a golden eagle crest on the flag

questions.explanation: A is correct. Subhadra's chariot is 'Darpadalana' (also spelled Debadalana), draped in black and red cloth, flying a Padma (lotus) flag. Option D (Garududhwaja — eagle flag) is the most tempting wrong answer because Garuda is Vishnu's vehicle, but that eagle emblem belongs to Jagannath's Nandighosha, not Subhadra's. 'Taladhwaja' means 'palm-tree flag' and is Balabhadra's chariot — a precise trivia chain that trips up most students.

questions.stem: The 'Bonderam Festival' of Goa — celebrated on Divar Island every fourth Saturday of August — features a colourful procession of flags called 'bonderas'. This spectacle originally re-enacted which episode from Goa's Portuguese colonial history?

options.option_text: Inter-village boundary disputes resolved by marker flags
The annual oath-taking ceremony of the Portuguese Viceroy
The first Portuguese flag-planting at Velha Goa's fortress
The Comunidade land-lottery redistribution unique to Goa

questions.explanation: A is correct. During Portuguese rule, Divar Island's hamlets had frequent boundary disputes; communities settled them by planting marker flags (bonderas) at contested points. The festival now cheerfully re-enacts this with mock battles and flag processions. Option D (Comunidade) is the most dangerous distractor — the Comunidade was a real Portuguese-era Goan village collective that managed land — but it has no connection to Bonderam's flag-planting tradition.

questions.stem: The 'Torgya' festival at Tawang Monastery (Arunachal Pradesh) — a three-day Buddhist celebration in January featuring elaborate Cham mask dances — culminates in the ritual burning of a 'torma' effigy. What does this burning primarily symbolise?

options.option_text: Elimination of evil spirits and negativity from the monastic region
Thanksgiving for the highland barley harvest of the Monpa community
Commemoration of the 6th Dalai Lama's birth at Urgelling, Tawang
Propitiation of pre-Buddhist Monpa forest deities during winter

questions.explanation: A is correct. The 'torma' is a ritual dough effigy representing accumulated negativity; its burning at Torgya's climax expels evil forces — a core Vajrayana Buddhist rite performed by Tawang's Gelugpa monks. Option C is the shrewdest distractor: Tsangyang Gyatso, the 6th Dalai Lama, was genuinely born at Urgelling Monastery near Tawang in 1683, making the Tawang connection historically real — but Torgya's purpose is protective, not commemorative of his birth.

questions.stem: The 'Chapchar Kut' festival — one of the most joyous spring festivals of Mizoram — is traditionally celebrated after the completion of which arduous agricultural task?

options.option_text: After completing the first rice transplantation in paddy fields
After clearing jungle for the start of shifting (jhum) cultivation
After the first maize harvest from community terraced farmland
After constructing community granaries and storing the crop yield

questions.explanation: B is correct. Chapchar Kut (held in February–March) celebrates the completion of the strenuous work of cutting and burning the forest undergrowth to prepare fields for jhum (shifting) cultivation — the festival is a joyful break before actual sowing begins. Option A (transplantation) is wrong because transplantation follows sowing, which comes after Chapchar Kut, not before it. Options C and D describe post-harvest activities unrelated to the festival's timing.

questions.stem: The 'Aranmula Uthrattathi Vallamkali' is unique among all Kerala boat races because it is not a competitive event but a sacred ritual procession. On which river is this ceremonial snake-boat event held?

options.option_text: Periyar River flowing through the Ernakulam district
Pamba River at Aranmula in Pathanamthitta district
Chaliyar River near the Beypore port in Kozhikode
Meenachil River passing through Kottayam's backwater belt

questions.explanation: B is correct. The Aranmula Vallamkali is held on the Pamba River at Aranmula, Pathanamthitta — it is a ritual offering (not a race) linked to the Parthasarathy temple and is considered a sacred vedic tradition. The common confusion is with the Nehru Trophy Boat Race (competitive), which is held on Punnamada Lake in Alappuzha. Options A, C, and D name rivers in other districts that have no connection to this festival.

questions.stem: The Hornbill Festival of Nagaland is held from 1 to 10 December each year at the Naga Heritage Village, Kisama. The specific choice of 1 December as the opening date commemorates which occasion?

options.option_text: Foundation of the Nagaland Legislative Assembly in 1964
Nagaland achieving full statehood on 1 December 1963
Birth anniversary of tribal freedom fighter Rani Gaidinliu
Signing of the Shillong Accord on Naga peace negotiations

questions.explanation: B is correct. Nagaland became the 16th state of India on 1 December 1963. The Hornbill Festival, launched in 2000 by the state government to revive Naga cultural heritage, was deliberately timed to begin on Statehood Day. Option A is wrong — the Legislative Assembly was constituted after statehood, not on this date. Option C is wrong — Rani Gaidinliu was born on 26 January 1915. Option D (Shillong Accord, 1975) is a different event entirely unrelated to the festival's calendar.

questions.stem: The Pushkar Camel Fair (Kartik Mela) is held annually in Rajasthan during Kartik Purnima. Which feature of Pushkar town makes it uniquely significant among major Hindu pilgrimage centres across India?

options.option_text: It is the only major pilgrimage town situated entirely within a desert
It houses the only major functioning temple dedicated to Lord Brahma
Its sacred lake has no surface river inlet — fed by underground springs
It is the only pilgrimage site awarded a UNESCO Intangible Heritage status

questions.explanation: B is correct. The Jagatpita Brahma Mandir at Pushkar is the only major, actively worshipped temple dedicated to Lord Brahma in India — mythology holds that a curse by Goddess Saraswati (or Gayatri) restricted Brahma's worship to this single site. Option A is incorrect — several pilgrimage towns (Dwarka, Rameshwaram) are in coastal or semi-arid zones. Option C is unverified and misleading. Option D is false — Pushkar has no UNESCO designation.

questions.stem: The 'Nanda Devi Raj Jat Yatra' — a foot pilgrimage of approximately 280 km through the Himalayan ranges of Uttarakhand — has which distinctive feature that sets it apart from other major Hindu pilgrimage yatras of India?

options.option_text: It is conducted exclusively by women priests from Kumaon hill villages
It is held only once every twelve years rather than annually
It is the only Himalayan yatra requiring central government security clearance
It is restricted by law to residents of Uttarakhand state only

questions.explanation: B is correct. The Nanda Devi Raj Jat Yatra (last held in 2014) is a 12-yearly pilgrimage revered by Garhwali and Kumaoni communities honouring Goddess Nanda Devi, state deity of Uttarakhand. A distinguishing ritual feature is that the procession is traditionally led by a naturally occurring chaurasingha (four-horned ram). Option A is wrong — it involves thousands of mixed-gender devotees, not exclusively women priests. Options C and D describe fabricated administrative restrictions with no basis in law or practice.

questions.stem: The 'Bhagoria Haat' festival — observed by the Bhil and Bhilala tribal communities of Madhya Pradesh — functions simultaneously as a weekly market and a customary occasion for partner selection under tribal law. This festival is held in the week immediately preceding which major Hindu festival?

options.option_text: Diwali — the festival of lights in the Hindu lunar calendar
Holi — the spring colour festival celebrated across India
Navratri — the nine-night festival honouring Goddess Durga
Makar Sankranti — the mid-January harvest festival of India

questions.explanation: B is correct. Bhagoria Haat is held across seven consecutive haat (market) days in Jhabua and Alirajpur districts during February–March, culminating just before Holi. Under tribal custom, a young man smearing gulal on a girl's cheek — and her acceptance — constitutes a public declaration of intent to marry (the word 'bhagoria' derives from 'bhagna' = to elope). Option A (Diwali, October–November) and D (Makar Sankranti, January) are wrong by season. Option C (Navratri) falls in autumn — entirely the wrong agricultural and ritual context.

questions.stem: The 'Bastar Dussehra' of Chhattisgarh — documented as the world's longest Dussehra celebration spanning 75 days — differs fundamentally from mainstream pan-Indian Dussehra because it does not celebrate Rama's victory over Ravana. It is instead primarily observed as the festival of which deity?

options.option_text: Lord Jagannath worshipped in a distinct Bastar regional tradition
Goddess Danteshwari — the presiding deity of the Bastar kingdom
Goddess Bhumia — the forest earth deity of the Gond tribal belt
Lord Shiva as Pashupati — patron deity of Chhattisgarh tribal clans

questions.explanation: B is correct. Bastar Dussehra centres on Goddess Danteshwari (a fierce Shakti form and kuldevi of the Bastar royal dynasty). The deity's idol is ceremonially brought from the Danteshwari temple at Dantewada to Jagdalpur, and the festival's rituals predate Ramayana-linked traditions. Option A (Jagannath) misleads because Jagannath is strongly associated with Odisha — the confusion is geographical. Option C (Bhumia) is a real Gond earth deity but not the presiding deity of Bastar Dussehra. Option D (Pashupati/Shiva) has no documented basis in this festival's tradition.
